summary.title: Health Network Asset Inventory
summary.description: This diagram will highlight all asset information found within the Health Network Infrastructure & its severity levels.

threats.title: Spoofing
threats.description: The Attacker impersonates a legitimate patient with credential stuffing. A phishing email spoofed to appear from "Epic Technical Support" tricks the user into opening a malicious attachment.
threats.mitigation: DMARC/SPF/DKIM implementation, email authentication, display external sender warnings, and anti-spoofing rules.

threats.title: Tampering
threats.description: An SQL injection attack allows an attacker to modify patient records, appointment data, or billing information
threats.mitigation: Input validation, parameterized queries, web application firewall (WAF), and regular security code reviews.

threats.title: Repuditation
threats.description: Insufficient logging of patient portal access allows users to deny actions (viewing records, making changes)
threats.mitigation: Comprehensive audit logging sent to Splunk SIEM, log integrity protection, and HIPAA-compliant access logs.

threats.title: Information Disclosure
threats.description: Weak session management or insecure direct object references expose PHI to unauthorized users.
threats.mitigation: Secure session tokens, HTTPS enforcement, proper authorization checks, and session timeout after inactivity.

threats.title: DDoS Attack
threats.description: A DDoS attack overwhelms the MyChart portal, making it unavailable to patients who need to access medical records.
threats.mitigation: DDoS protection via Palo Alto firewall, rate limiting, CDN with DDoS protection, and load balancing.

threats.title: Elevation of Privlege
threats.description: Path traversal or broken access control allows patient users to access administrative functions or other patients' data.
threats.mitigation: Principle of least privilege, role-based access control (RBAC), input sanitization, and regular penetration testing.

threats.title: Shadow copies deleted via vsadmin [TAMPERING]
threats.description: Ransomware deleted shadow copies using the vssadmin account and the delete shadows /all /quiet command
threats.mitigation: Restrict vssadmin access, monitor for shadow copy deletion, application whitelisting, and backup server isolation.

threats.title: Backup Server encrypted by ransomware
threats.description: The backup server was encrypted by ransomware, making recovery operations impossible during the incident.
threats.mitigation: Air-gapped backups, immutable backup storage with correct 30-day configuration, offline tape backups, separate backup network.

threats.title: Backup Retention misconfigured to 7 days.
threats.description: An immutable backup misconfigured with 7-day retention instead of 30-day retention exposes the organization to data loss.
threats.mitigation: Quarterly backup configuration audits, automated configuration validation, documented backup procedures, and regular restore testing.

threats.title: Compromised Backup admin credentials
threats.description: Compromised backup administrator credentials provide access to all backup data and the ability to delete backups
threats.mitigation: Separate backup admin accounts, MFA for backup access, privileged access management, and audit backup administrator actions

threats.title: Stolen VPN Credentials for unauthorized access
threats.description: Stolen VPN credentials used for unauthorized remote access to the internal network
threats.mitigation: MFA enabled for all VPN access (reduces risk), certificate-based authentication, and monitors VPN connections for anomalies.

threats.title: Pass-the-hash Attack with stolen NTLM hashes.
threats.description: Pass-the-hash attack using stolen NTLM hashes allows an attacker to authenticate as legitimate users without knowing passwords
threats.mitigation: Disable NTLM where possible, implement Kerberos, credential guard, protected users group, reduce local admin rights.

threats.title: Domain Admin creds from lsass dump
threats.description: Domain admin credentials were harvested from memory using lsass.exe dump on the compromised workstation.
threats.mitigation: Credential Guard, protected process for lsass, no domain admin logins to workstations, tiered administration model.

threats.title: Group Policy modified to disable defender
threats.description: Attacker modifies Group Policy to disable Windows Defender across the entire domain.
threats.mitigation: Protected GPO objects, least privilege for GPO modification, GPO change auditing, and backup domain controllers.

threats.title: Domain Admin provides unrestricted access
threats.description: Domain administrator credentials provide unrestricted access to all systems in the network, enabling lateral movement.
threats.mitigation: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs), just-in-time admin access, reduce the number of domain admins, and monitor privileged account usage.

threats.title: Spoofing
threats.description: Service account credentials were stolen and used to authenticate as a legitimate database service.
threats.mitigation: Implement Privileged Access Management (PAM), service account credential rotation, and monitor for abnormal service account usage.

threats.title: Ransomware
threats.description: Ransomware encrypts 50GB database files containing 50,000+ patient records, making them inaccessible.
threats.mitigation: Network segmentation, EDR on database servers, immutable backups with proper configuration (30-day retention), and offline backup copies.

threats.title: 50,000 + PHI records exfiltrated
threats.description: 50,000+ PHI records exfiltrated to attacker C2 infrastructure before encryption
threats.mitigation: Data Loss Prevention (DLP), network traffic monitoring, encryption at rest, database activity monitoring, egress filtering.

threats.title: Database Encryption prevents patient care
threats.description: Database corruption or encryption prevents patient care systems from accessing critical medical information
threats.mitigation: Database redundancy/clustering, tested backup and restore procedures, disaster recovery plan, RTO/RPO documentation.

threats.title: SQL Injection for administrative access
threats.description: SQL injection or compromised application credentials allow unauthorized administrative access to the database.
threats.mitigation: Implement the principle of least privilege for database accounts, disable xp_cmdshell, implement input validation, enable database firewall rules, and conduct regular vulnerability scanning.
